I used to have this recurring dream as a kid through my early teenage years where I would be in my grandmother's old house and I couldn't find anyone. One day I just stopped having them like 10 years ago.

I don't usually remember my dreams. Most of them are gone by the morning. However, one stood out for some reason. It's not particularly strange or scary, but it was so...vivid in my memory when I woke up.

I was in a canoe with 3 of my friends, paddling down a river. The river banks were very tall and steep, probably 10 feet or so. Any time there was a bend in the river, you couldn't see what was around the corner. The walls of the river obscured everything. We just kept paddling, around every bend, until we saw it. The House of Thorns.

The house was not made of thorns. It didn't even have much thorn-like architecture. But it had a bigass sign above the entrance that told us it was called the House of Thorns. Being a bunch of invincible 20 somethings that are oblivious to the obvious horror movie this is turning into, we go inside.

Turns out, this is a haunted house. In fact, it is the greatest haunted house in the world, despite nobody ever hearing about it before now. And best of all, admission is free, since they haven't had customers in a while. Again, dream me and my friends don't realize this is a great way to meet an chainsaw face-to-face, so we go for it.

The first floor has us ride in little cars, kinda like the Haunted Mansion ride at Disney World. Pretty benign stuff. Ghosts, moving furniture, creepy noises. Obviously not the best haunted house in the world. The car takes us up the stairs and drops us off a the second floor.

This floor is a walking tour. After taking a couple steps, the scenery melts away, and it is revealed that the stairs were actually a portal to a different plane of existence. This place is rocky, and the stars in the night sky give everything a bluish tint. Some sorta goblin/dinosaur dude runs up to us, and turns out to be our guide through this part of the house. The place resembled the Oblivion plane from the Elder Scrolls games, but less volcanoes and lava. It was creepy, in that we had no clue what we were doing on an alternate plane of existence, but again, rather benign for "the scariest haunted house in the world".

We get to the end of this part of the tour, and end up on the roof of the house. There's a structure that looks kinda like a chimney, but probably 10'x10' in cross section, that tunneled through the entire house, presumably into the basement, but it was too dark to see all the way down. The outside walls of this chimney are covered in thorny vines made of iron, or some other dark metal. Our guide tells us that the last part of our tour was the "Thorns Level", and to get to it, we had to jump down the chimney. There would be a net at the bottom to catch us. The Thorns Level is the reason this place has its reputation as the scariest haunted house in the world. For the third time, we are given a clear warning that we are the stars in a horror movie. For the third time, we just roll with it.

I was the last one to jump in, so I watch my 3 friends climb up the chimney, then jump down. I never heard a thump, so obviously the net caught them. It gets to my turn, I climb up the chimney, look down, and jump.

You know those moments where you fall in a dream, and your actual body gets a falling sensation, so you wake up? That how this dream ended. I guess my brain realized that it wasn't creative enough to make a legit level for a haunted house, so it pressed the abort button and woke me up.
